# Story 01 — Ticket reports (volume, trends, category, source)

## Prerequisites

- ticket-management Story 63 completed: **`Ticket.createdVia`** (`customer_portal | ai | phone | email | in_person | other`) is persisted on every ticket, including backfill of pre-existing records.
- ticket-management Stories 8–13 completed: category, status, and the base `Ticket` model are stable.
- No sibling report plans exist yet in `.squad/plans/`; this is the first of the reports-management stories (39–43). Establish the reusable aggregation + filter parsing pattern here — Stories 40 (SLA), 41 (agent perf), 42 (CSAT), 43 (dashboard) will build on it.
- Read `CLAUDE.md` at the repo root before starting (permission model, list-view conventions, filter-wiring convention, "every route needs a permission" rule).

---

## Story Goal

Give admins a **Ticket Reports** page under `/admin/reports/tickets` that answers three questions:

1. **How many tickets did we handle in a given period, broken down by day / week / month?** (Trend view — chart + table.)
2. **What kinds of tickets were they?** (Category breakdown — table + share.)
3. **Where did they come from?** (Source breakdown by `createdVia`, reusing the existing labels + colours.)

The page must be filterable by **date range** and **category**, support **day/week/month grouping** for the trend view, and expose a **CSV export** of the currently-filtered dataset.

**Out of scope (state this explicitly on the page):**
- SLA metrics (Story 40), agent performance (Story 41), CSAT (Story 42), unified dashboard (Story 43).
- Live-chat volume as a separate channel — the report is scoped to `Ticket` rows only. An escalated chat that becomes a ticket appears once, via its `createdVia` value (typically `ai` on escalation, per Story 19 wiring — executor to confirm on the escalation service before writing the copy).
- **PDF export.** See "New-dependency decisions" below.

## Backend Tasks

### 1 — Create `backend/src/services/report.service.ts`

Central place for report aggregation building blocks that Stories 40–43 can reuse.

Exports (initial surface):

```ts
export type ReportGrouping = "day" | "week" | "month";

export interface TicketReportFilters {
  from: Date;         // inclusive
  to: Date;           // exclusive (normalise callers to end-of-day + 1ms)
  categoryIds?: string[]; // ObjectId strings; empty/undefined = all
}

export interface TicketVolumePoint {
  bucket: string;     // ISO date for day; ISO week start for week; YYYY-MM for month
  count: number;
}

export interface TicketCategoryBreakdownRow {
  categoryId: string | null;   // null = tickets with no category
  categoryName: { en: string; ar: string } | null;
  count: number;
}

export interface TicketSourceBreakdownRow {
  createdVia: TicketCreationChannel | null; // null bucket for legacy pre-Story-63 rows
  count: number;
}

export interface TicketReport {
  totals: { count: number };
  trend: TicketVolumePoint[];
  byCategory: TicketCategoryBreakdownRow[];
  bySource: TicketSourceBreakdownRow[];
  filters: TicketReportFilters & { grouping: ReportGrouping };
}

export async function buildTicketReport(
  input: TicketReportFilters & { grouping: ReportGrouping }
): Promise<TicketReport>;
```

Implementation notes:

- Use a single `Ticket.aggregate([...])` pipeline that emits all three breakdowns via `$facet` so we make one round-trip per request:
  - `$match`: `{ createdAt: { $gte: from, $lt: to }, ...(categoryIds ? { category: { $in: [...ObjectIds] } } : {}) }`.
  - `$facet` branches: `trend` (uses `$dateTrunc` with unit derived from `grouping`), `byCategory` (`$group` on `category`, then `$lookup` into `ticketcategories` for the localised name), `bySource` (`$group` on `createdVia`), `totals` (`$count`).
- **Null-safe:** if `createdVia` is `null` (pre-Story-63 rows escaped backfill), still surface them as a `null` bucket — do not drop them silently, or totals won't reconcile.
- Cap `to - from` at a hard maximum (e.g. **370 days**) to keep the aggregation bounded; return a 400 in the route if exceeded.
- Add a helper `parseReportFilters(query: unknown): TicketReportFilters & { grouping }` used by both the JSON and CSV route to guarantee identical semantics.

## Product rules (from story)

- **Current behaviour:** No ticket-volume report exists in the app. Ticket source, category, and date are visible only per-ticket in the queue.
- **New behaviour:** Admins can open `/admin/reports/tickets`, pick a date range + category filter + grouping, and see totals, a trend chart, a category breakdown, and a source breakdown. They can download the current filtered view as CSV.

---

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Empty range** (`from == to` or `from > to`): backend validation rejects with 400 `"invalid_date_range"`. Frontend filter bar prevents submission with an inline error and does not fire the fetch.
- **Range > 370 days:** backend returns 400 `"range_too_large"`; frontend shows an inline toast and clamps the picker.
- **Category id that no longer exists:** aggregation returns zero rows for it; the response still includes an entry for it with `count: 0` and `categoryName: null`. Frontend renders "Deleted category".
- **Tickets with `createdVia == null`** (legacy rows Story 63 missed): show up in the `null` bucket in `bySource`; total count reconciles with `totals.count`. **Do not drop them.**
- **Timezone:** `$dateTrunc` uses UTC by default. Document this once in the page footer ("Times are UTC"). Do not attempt per-user timezone in this story — flag as follow-up.
- **DST when `grouping = "week"`:** weeks start Monday UTC to avoid DST edge cases. Assert this in the trend test.
- **Non-admin session with a stale sidebar link:** server component re-checks `reports.tickets.view` and renders the "no access" page — front-end nav visibility alone is not sufficient (per the permission-audit gotcha in memory: role short-circuits must also honour `isActive`).
- **Deactivated admin** (`isActive = false`): `requireAuth` must reject before `requirePermission` runs. Verify against `backend/src/middleware/auth.ts` and add an integration test covering it.
- **CSV export on a very large range:** worst case 370 days × N buckets is small; the aggregation is bounded by cardinality of `bySource` (≤ 7) and `byCategory` (≤ total categories). No streaming needed for this story; if a future story raises the range cap, revisit.
- **Concurrent export clicks:** browser handles as separate GETs; server has no shared state. Fine.
- **Unicode/RTL in category names:** CSV writes UTF-8 with BOM (`\uFEFF`) so Excel opens Arabic names correctly. Assert in the CSV test.

## Migration / Rollback

- **No schema change.** No migration script.
- Permission keys are additive; a rollback (revert of `permissions.ts` + route removal) leaves data untouched.
- If `recharts` is later swapped out, only `TicketTrendChart.tsx` changes.
- **Half-applied state:** if the backend ships without the frontend, the nav entry does not appear (permission gate + no link). If the frontend ships without the backend, the fetch returns 404 and the page renders the empty state with a "Report unavailable" error banner — verify by temporarily commenting out the route mount before merging.

## Deviations from this plan (scout ran out of budget before verifying these — corrected during implementation against the real codebase)

- **Reused the existing `reports:view` / `reports:export` permission keys** (already defined in `backend/src/constants/permissions.ts`, already agent-grantable via `DEFAULT_PERMISSIONS_BY_ROLE`) instead of adding new `reports.tickets.view` / `reports.tickets.export` keys — the plan's scout couldn't read that file before the budget ran out, so it assumed the keys didn't exist. Not admin-only: an agent granted `reports:view` can view; `reports:export` is subadmin-tier per the existing `SUBADMIN_ONLY_PERMISSIONS` set.
- **No `$lookup` for category names** — `Ticket.category` is a plain string snapshot, not an ObjectId reference (see `backend/src/models/TicketCategory.ts`'s doc comment), so `byCategory` groups directly on the string.
- **No `recharts` dependency** — used a small shared inline-SVG component (`frontend/components/reports/TimeSeriesBarChart.tsx`, also used by the SLA report) instead, consistent with the SLA report's own (successfully-scouted) plan explicitly avoiding a new charting dependency.
- **No audit-log entry on CSV export** — same reasoning the SLA plan gives explicitly: report reads/exports aren't mutations under the current audit contract, and logging them would require extending the fixed `AUDIT_TARGET_TYPES` enum for no real security benefit.
- **Routes live under `/api/v1/reports/...`** (versioned, per `CLAUDE.md`), not `/api/reports/...`.
- **No PDF export button rendered at all** (not even disabled) — simplified from "disabled with tooltip" to omitted entirely; the CSV button and this plan's own PDF-deferral note make the gap clear without a dead control on the page.
- **Category filter is a single-select**, not a multi-select — every other filter bar in this codebase (audit logs, tickets) uses a single-value `Select`; there's no existing multi-select convention to reuse, so this matches precedent instead of inventing one. The backend query schema still accepts one-or-many for forward compatibility.
- Shared `/admin/reports` layout + tab strip built alongside this story (`layout.tsx`, `ReportsTabs.tsx`) rather than a separate landing page, since Story 41 (SLA) needed the same shell.
